subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: How should maintainers split and own #86567 across durable dashboard auth recovery, OpenAI/Codex auth propagation, runtime/update atomicity, final-turn liveness, and context hygiene?
rationale: The issue mixes security-sensitive credential persistence, installer/runtime guarantees, provider migration policy, and session behavior; automation cannot choose the permanent ownership boundaries or credential durability policy safely.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split focused owners
options.body: Keep #86567 open as a coordination tracker while linking or creating focused canonical issues/PRs for dashboard auth, provider auth, runtime atomicity, final-turn liveness, and context hygiene.

options.title: Replace with narrower canonical issues
options.body: Close this umbrella only after maintainers create and link complete narrower canonical issues that preserve every still-missing acceptance criterion.

options.title: Defer non-auth improvements
options.body: Treat auth/install blockers as immediate work and explicitly defer long-session context hygiene into roadmap planning.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split focused owners
recommendation.body: Keep #86567 open as a coordination tracker while linking or creating focused canonical issues/PRs for dashboard auth, provider auth, runtime atomicity, final-turn liveness, and context hygiene.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent overlap across the dashboard, provider/auth, docs, and session-runtime surfaces involved in the split decision.
